protocol.question: Are the Future Wealth return models calibrated out of sample, and does any beat a normal (Gaussian i.i.d.) baseline?
protocol.decision_rule: A model beats the baseline only if its mean CRPS is lower and a Diebold-Mariano test (Newey-West variance with h-1 lags, Harvey-Leybourne-Newbold small-sample correction, t p-values) rejects equality at 5% after Holm adjustment across the models tested at that portfolio, horizon and window. No test is attempted with fewer than 20 non-overlapping outcomes.
protocol.history_of_this_protocol: The minimum-outcome rule and the small-sample correction were added after the --synthetic pipeline check produced false 'wins' at 36 months on i.i.d. normal data, and before the real snapshot was evaluated.

notes: SYNTHETIC GBM seed=11; not market data

conclusions: 1-month horizon, rolling 60 months (345 non-overlapping outcomes): iid_bootstrap, block_bootstrap, ewma_filtered are significantly WORSE than the normal baseline. 90% interval coverage: iid_bootstrap 89%, block_bootstrap 89%, ewma_filtered 90%, gaussian_iid 90%.

1-month horizon, expanding (345 non-overlapping outcomes): iid_bootstrap, block_bootstrap, ewma_filtered are significantly WORSE than the normal baseline. 90% interval coverage: iid_bootstrap 88%, block_bootstrap 88%, ewma_filtered 89%, gaussian_iid 89%.

1-month horizon, rolling 120 months (285 non-overlapping outcomes): iid_bootstrap, block_bootstrap, ewma_filtered did not differ significantly from the normal baseline; the extra complexity is not supported by this evidence. 90% interval coverage: iid_bootstrap 88%, block_bootstrap 88%, ewma_filtered 88%, gaussian_iid 88%.

12-month horizon, rolling 60 months (28 non-overlapping outcomes): iid_bootstrap, block_bootstrap, ewma_filtered did not differ significantly from the normal baseline; the extra complexity is not supported by this evidence. 90% interval coverage: iid_bootstrap 88%, block_bootstrap 77%, ewma_filtered 90%, gaussian_iid 88%.
